# Workflow steps

A workflow (`operation.multi_step`) is a list of steps, each `{step_id, operation_id, spec, depends_on}`. These are the step operations and their `spec` fields. Steps that only read data run without a confirmation click (see the Agent chapter).

Reported percentiles: 1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 75, 90, 95, 99.

## `data.aggregate`

| `aggregations` | yes | Named aggregation declarations. |

## `data.append`

Append a declared secondary dataset with an explicit schema policy. Example spec: {"schema_policy": "exact", "secondary_artifact_id": "raw_b.csv", "secondary_node_id": "stage:raw", "secondary_run_id": "run_b"}

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `secondary_run_id` | yes | Real run id for the secondary dataset, discovered from project evidence. |
| `secondary_node_id` | yes | Real graph node id for the secondary dataset. |
| `secondary_artifact_id` | yes | Real artifact-index id for the secondary dataset. |
| `schema_policy` |  | Schema policy: exact or union. |
| `row_growth_policy` |  | Explicit row-growth bound. |
| `max_growth_factor` |  | Legacy growth-factor bound. |

## `data.dedupe`

| `columns` | yes | Deduplication key columns. |
| `keep` | yes | first or last occurrence. |

## `data.merge`

Merge the current dataset with a declared secondary dataset. Example spec: {"how": "left", "keys": ["id"], "secondary_artifact_id": "raw_b.csv", "secondary_node_id": "stage:raw", "secondary_run_id": "run_b"}

| `secondary_artifact_id` | yes | Real artifact-index id for the secondary dataset. |
| `keys` | yes | Non-empty join-key column list present in both datasets. |
| `how` |  | Join mode: left, right, inner, or outer. |
| `indicator` |  | Optional true or a non-empty output-column name. |
| `growth_policy` |  | Explicit row-growth bound. |
| `max_growth_factor` |  | Legacy growth-factor bound. |

## `data.recode`

Recode one variable into a NEW variable by ordered rules (SPSS RECODE INTO): single values, closed numeric ranges {low, high}, "missing", and a final "else". First matching rule wins; to: a code, null (missing) or "copy". Values no rule covers are refused unless an else rule exists. Example spec: {"column": "age", "output": "age_group", "rules": [{"from": {"high": 39, "low": 18}, "to": 1}, {"from": {"high": 120, "low": 40}, "to": 2}, {"from": "missing", "to": 9}]}

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `column` | yes | Existing source column; it is not changed. |
| `output` | yes | Name of the new variable; must not exist yet. |
| `rules` | yes | Ordered list of {from, to}. |

|---|---|---|

| `index` |  | Index columns for long_to_wide. |
| `columns` |  | Long-form column containing wide labels. |
| `values` |  | Long-form value column. |
| `var_name` |  | Output variable-name column for wide_to_long. |
| `value_name` |  | Output value column for wide_to_long. |

## `model.genesis`

Estimate one or more models from the source table.

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `model_family` | yes | Registered workflow-executable model family: anova, cs_did, dcdh, did, glm:binomial, glm:negative_binomial, glm:poisson, iv_2sls, linear_mixed_effects, logit, multinomial_logit, negative_binomial, ols, ordinal_logit, panel_ols, poisson, probit, quantile_regression, sa_did, survival_cox. Every branch in one step uses this same family. |
| `covariance` |  | Default covariance for every branch. panel_ols and did cluster by entity when omitted (CR1, t(G-1), as Stata's xtreg, fe vce(robust)); to cluster at the level where treatment was assigned, name that column in model_options.cluster. robust (not clustered) is inconsistent with a fixed number of periods; offer it only to reproduce earlier work. |
| `model_options` |  | Family-owned JSON options. Only the selected model family's declared option fields are accepted; do not copy options from another family. |
| `entity_col` |  | Panel entity column. panel_ols requires entity_col or time_col; clustered panel covariance requires entity_col. |
| `time_col` |  | Optional panel time column for time fixed effects. |
| `cohort_col` |  | First-treatment period for cs_did or sa_did (0 for never treated). |
| `treatment_path_col` |  | Binary treatment path for dcdh, which may switch on and off. |
| `iv_endog` |  | Non-empty endogenous-regressor column list for iv_2sls. |
| `iv_instruments` |  | Non-empty instrument column list for iv_2sls; must not overlap endog or predictors. |
| `did_mode` |  | TWFE DID treatment definition: cohort, two_by_two, or status. |
| `did_cohort_col` |  | First-treatment period for did_mode cohort (0 for never treated). |
| `did_treat_col` |  | Treatment-group indicator for did_mode two_by_two. |
| `did_post_col` |  | Post-period indicator for did_mode two_by_two. |
| `did_status_col` |  | Absorbing treatment-status indicator for did_mode status. |
| `survey_strata_col` |  | Survey strata column. |
| `survey_psu_col` |  | Survey PSU column. |
| `survey_fpc_col` |  | Finite population correction column. |
| `survey_replicate_weights` |  | Replicate weight columns. |
| `survey_replicate_type` |  | Replicate method. One of: brr, jackknife, bootstrap, provided. |
| `survey_lonely_psu` |  | Single-PSU stratum policy. One of: fail, remove, adjust, average, certainty. |
| `survey_weight_frame` |  | Panel weight frame. One of: cross_sectional, longitudinal. |
| `survey_subpop` |  | Subpopulation condition. |
| `survey_df` |  | Coefficient test degrees of freedom. One of: design, design_minus_p. |
| `sampling_weight` |  | Column holding the sampling weight. A survey design requires one, and a sampling weight without a declared design is refused -- give both or neither. |
| `labels` |  | Column metadata. `measurement_level` maps column names to nominal / ordinal / scale / count and decides how each column is modelled -- an integer rating left undeclared is analysed as a count. Declare every column in one step rather than one at a time. |
| `branches` | yes | List of {branch_id, outcome, predictors[, categorical][, polynomials][, covariance]}; one estimated model per entry. Entries in `predictors` enter LINEARLY, exactly as the column stands — listing a categorical code column there estimates a linear effect on the code, which is a different model. Use `categorical` for dummy expansion and `polynomials` for powers. Interaction terms cannot be expressed; say so rather than approximating one. |
| `categorical` |  | Per branch: list of column names to expand into dummy indicators. One level is dropped as the reference category to avoid perfect collinearity with the intercept; the lowest sorted level is the reference. A column listed here must NOT also appear in `predictors`. |
| `polynomials` |  | Per branch: list of {column, degree}. degree 2 adds the square, 3 adds square and cube, and so on; generated columns are named {column}_pow2, {column}_pow3. The linear term is not added implicitly — list the column in `predictors` as well when the model should contain it. |
| `context_columns` |  | Extra columns to carry into the model context. |
| `multiple_imputations` |  | Optional m (2-100) for multiple imputation: missing values in the outcome and predictors are imputed m times by chained equations (MICE), the model is fitted to each completed dataset, and the estimates are pooled by Rubin's rules with Barnard-Rubin degrees of freedom. Offered for: ols with covariance unadjusted, robust or clustered; logit (its model-based covariance). Refused with a sampling design. Pooled results report no R-squared or residual diagnostics, and joint tests on them are not available yet. |
| `by_group` |  | Optional grouping column: the model is estimated separately within each group (a missing value is a group of its own; at most 50 groups; under a sampling design each group is a domain of the full design). Each group gets its own result; a group below the check library's sample minimum is listed as not estimable. The run also tests whether the groups' coefficients differ (Wald on the fully interacted pooled model): cite that test before saying groups differ. Offered for: logit, ols, poisson, probit. |

## `model.joint_f_test`

Test whether one or more declared OLS term groups are jointly zero. Selectors can reference only linear predictors, categorical dummy sets, or generated polynomial powers that the dependent model branch already declared.

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `branch_id` | yes | Declared model branch to read from a direct dependency. |
| `term_selectors` | yes | Non-empty list of {kind, column}; kind is linear, categorical, or polynomial. `column` is a source column, not a generated coefficient name or formula fragment. |

## `model.quadratic_stationary_point`

Compute the stationary point of one declared linear-plus-square term in a completed unadjusted OLS branch.

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `branch_id` | yes | Declared model branch to read from a direct dependency. |
| `column` | yes | Source column declared both as a linear predictor and as a degree-two polynomial term. |

## `postestimation.lincom`

Estimate a linear combination of a completed model's coefficients, with its standard error, test and confidence interval. Offered for: did, glm:binomial, glm:negative_binomial, glm:poisson, iv_2sls, linear_mixed_effects, logit, multinomial_logit, negative_binomial, ols, ordinal_logit, panel_ols, poisson, probit, the families where it has been checked against a reference implementation; for any other family say it is not offered yet because that check is missing, not because the model cannot. Plan the workflow on the dataset node the model was estimated from (its parent stage, such as stage:cleaned), not on the model node; name the model in model_ref.

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `model_ref` | yes | Model node to read, as shown in the graph (`model:logit_1`, or its forest key); the model must belong to `model_run_id`, or to the workflow's target run when that is omitted. For a model fitted earlier in this same plan, use `step:<step_id>:<branch_id>`; the named producer declares that branch, and its dependency is added automatically. Do not guess a future run id or model node id. |
| `model_run_id` |  | Run that owns `model_ref`; omit it for the workflow's target run. |
| `terms` | yes | Object mapping coefficient names to weights. |
| `constant` |  | Number added to the combination, default 0. |
| `level` |  | Confidence level, default 0.95. |

## `postestimation.lr`

Likelihood-ratio test of a restricted model nested in a fuller one. Both must be estimated on the same rows with model-based (not robust or clustered) variance. If the user's original model has robust, clustered or design-based variance, explain that LR uses the model likelihood and requires two new fits with model-based variance; keep the original model and actively offer a Wald test using its original covariance as an alternative. Do not automatically add a Wald step merely because the user asks you to offer that option; include it only when execution of Wald is requested. Fit both branches and then reference them in one plan with one confirmation. Offered for: glm:binomial, glm:negative_binomial, glm:poisson, logit, ols, poisson, probit, the families where it has been checked against a reference implementation; for any other family say it is not offered yet because that check is missing, not because the model cannot. Plan the workflow on the dataset node the model was estimated from (its parent stage, such as stage:cleaned), not on the model node; name the model in model_ref.

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `model_ref` | yes | The fuller model. Model node to read, as shown in the graph (`model:logit_1`, or its forest key); the model must belong to `model_run_id`, or to the workflow's target run when that is omitted. For a model fitted earlier in this same plan, use `step:<step_id>:<branch_id>`; the named producer declares that branch, and its dependency is added automatically. Do not guess a future run id or model node id. |
| `model_run_id` |  | Run that owns `model_ref`; omit it for the workflow's target run. |
| `restricted_model_ref` | yes | The restricted model nested in it. Model node to read, as shown in the graph (`model:logit_1`, or its forest key); the model must belong to `model_run_id`, or to the workflow's target run when that is omitted. For a model fitted earlier in this same plan, use `step:<step_id>:<branch_id>`; the named producer declares that branch, and its dependency is added automatically. Do not guess a future run id or model node id. |
| `restricted_model_run_id` |  | Run that owns the restricted model; omit for the target run. |

## `postestimation.wald`

Jointly test linear restrictions on a completed model's coefficients (Wald). Reads the model's stored covariance; F or chi-square follows the model's own inference. Offered for: did, glm:binomial, glm:negative_binomial, glm:poisson, iv_2sls, linear_mixed_effects, logit, multinomial_logit, negative_binomial, ols, ordinal_logit, panel_ols, poisson, probit, the families where it has been checked against a reference implementation; for any other family say it is not offered yet because that check is missing, not because the model cannot. Plan the workflow on the dataset node the model was estimated from (its parent stage, such as stage:cleaned), not on the model node; name the model in model_ref.

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `model_ref` | yes | Model node to read, as shown in the graph (`model:logit_1`, or its forest key); the model must belong to `model_run_id`, or to the workflow's target run when that is omitted. For a model fitted earlier in this same plan, use `step:<step_id>:<branch_id>`; the named producer declares that branch, and its dependency is added automatically. Do not guess a future run id or model node id. |
| `model_run_id` |  | Run that owns `model_ref`; omit it for the workflow's target run. |
| `constraints` | yes | Non-empty list of {terms, value}: `terms` maps coefficient names to weights and the restriction is sum(weight * coefficient) = value. Joint significance of x1 and x2 is [{terms: {x1: 1}, value: 0}, {terms: {x2: 1}, value: 0}]. |
